advice: Propose an unmaterialized-A SME path for every positive n. Keep the existing NN LIBXSMM call for n=512 as the control path. In the general-size path, compute 2VL×2VL output tiles with four ZA accumulators. For each K step, gather the tile’s A values from row-major A at rows i…i+2VL−1 and column k; load the matching contiguous B values at row k and columns j…j+2VL−1; then issue the four FP32 outer products and store the tile. This removes the full A transpose buffer and its allocation, conversion, and free. It is a distinct algorithm/layout change from both the existing transpose-then-SME fallback and the measured fixed-size TB wrappers. The hypothesis is that avoiding the materialized transpose can reduce total call cost; repeated strided A gathers may instead cost more. Treat the effect as unknown advice, not a measured result.
risks: A gathers may have poor locality and repeat A reads across column tiles. Tail masks must cover partial row and column tiles, and n<=0 must remain a no-op. Preserve FP32 operations and tolerance, fresh inputs, complete C overwrite, the ABI, single-thread setting, compiler flags, and license notices. Check sizes around VL and tile boundaries, odd tails, zero and negative n, input preservation, and allocation behavior. For n=512, require ten validation reports and ten fresh alternating paired controls with the frozen best-of-three rule; report historical and fresh same-mode peaks separately. Apply the unchanged promotion gate and held-out check. Include all gather, SME, and store work in timing. No performance gain or goal completion is established.
